column1: # Astrion Assistant — how people actually ask for things.
# phrase<TAB>the intent it should route to
# Generated by a language model asked to paraphrase each request the way a real
# person types it: casual, terse, polite, indirect. That is the ONE job a big
# model is genuinely good at here, and it is also the job that needs checking —
# so nothing in this file is trusted. tools/intent_probe.c runs every line
# through the real am_classify/am_action_of and reports which ones Astrion
# drops or misroutes. Those are the gaps.
# Lines are deliberately NOT all achievable. A corpus that only contains
# phrasings the matcher already handles measures nothing.
how much memory do i have
how much ram does this have
how long have you been running
how long has this been on
show me what you can do
how many files do i have
add bye to the end of notes.txt
make a copy of notes.txt called backup.txt
# "open notes.txt" lives here and not under file.read, which is where it was
# first written. The matcher routes it to app.open, wm.c finds no app by that
# name, and it opens the FILE in the Editor — which is what a person asking to
# "open" a file wants, better than printing it into the chat.
# This is the ONE line whose expectation moved instead of the code, so it is
# the one that needed the most proof. "the code is right and the corpus is
# wrong" is how a suite becomes a rubber stamp. It was not argued, it was
# booted: tools/intent_live_test.py types `open readme.txt` into a running
# Astrion and requires the Editor window to appear with no reply text.
i want to use the editor
# ROUND 2 — added 2026-08-09, after round 1 went from 82.3% to 100%.
# A corpus the matcher scores 100% on measures NOTHING. That is the rule this
# file opens with, and hitting 100% is the moment it stops being a measurement
# and becomes a rubber stamp. So round 1 stays (it is the regression net) and
# these are the new frontier: phrasings written WITHOUT looking at what the
# matcher handles, aimed at the questions a stranger asks in the first two
# minutes and at the words nobody thought to put in a keyword list.
# Expect this section to fail. That is its job. The number it produces is the
# honest coverage number, and the misses are the next round of work.
# ── the questions a stranger asks first ──
how does any of this work
am i running out of memory
will my files survive a reboot
how many files are on here
i need a file called ideas.txt
# The two below are the only lines in this file the matcher still gets wrong,
# and both are LEFT wrong on purpose. Written down rather than deleted, because
# a corpus that quietly drops what it cannot do is a corpus that reads 100%.
#   "i want to write something" routes to file.write, and wm.c finds no " to "
#   in it and falls through to the honest menu. Making it open the Editor would
#   mean claiming a sentence with no app name and no filename in it; the near
#   miss is "open the editor with something in it", and getting that wrong
#   writes a file the user never named.
#   "gaming time" routes to date, because DATE owns the word "time" and runs
#   long before anything about apps. Fixing it means weakening the branch that
#   answers "what time is it" — a common question — to catch a rare one.
